lines.S1: finally runs exactly once per entry of the try
lines.S2: a return inside the body or the handler is held, the block runs, then the held exit resumes
lines.S3: a raise inside the body or the handler is held, the block runs, then the held exit resumes
lines.S4: a raise (or a return) inside finally replaces a held exit
lines.S5: exit and loop crossing a try run its finally first

cases.why: the normal path: the body, the finally, then on
a raise in the body, caught: the handler, then the finally
a raise in the body with no catch: the finally, then the raise resumes outward
a return in the body: the value is taken, the finally runs (computing as it likes), the value returned is the one taken
a return in the handler: the finally runs, then the return resumes
a raise in the handler: the finally runs, then the raise resumes outward
cases.stdout:
finally after handler raise
outer: in handler

cases.why: `exit` crossing a try in a for loop runs its finally first
`loop` crossing a try in a for loop runs its finally first, and the loop goes on
cases.stdout:
body 1
finally 1
end 1
finally 2
body 3
finally 3
end 3

cases.why: `exit` crossing a try with a catch, in a while loop
a return crossing two trys runs the inner finally, then the outer
`exit 2` crossing two loops and two trys runs both finallys, inner first, once each
a raise in the finally on the return path goes outward: the finally does not run twice
a raise in the finally on the exit path never lands in the same try's catch
a try inside the finally does not overwrite the error the finally holds
a return in the finally replaces a held return
a return in the finally replaces a held raise
`exit` crossing a try in a for-in loop
`loop` crossing a try in a do-again loop
a return from a loop inside the try body runs the finally once
a return crossing a try without finally inside one with: both handlers are left, and a later raise lands where it is raised
